description: OPENS A FILE PICKER RIGHT HERE, in this conversation: the user presses a button, chooses a video OR PHOTO from their own computer and watches it upload, and then it is on their aicut account for every tool. No link, nothing to paste. CALL IT IMMEDIATELY, WITHOUT ASKING ANYTHING FIRST, the moment the user refers to a video or image file on their machine ('upscale the clip in my Downloads', 'use the picture on my desktop as the character'): do not ask for a path, size, format or URL, the picker asks for the file. A photo attached in chat does not reach aicut: ask the user to choose it again in the picker. WHEN NOT: the file is already a URL (public https, or from an earlier generation): pass it straight to the tool that needs it (uploading first stores the bytes twice against the allowance). Also not when you can run a shell command on their machine and no card renders (a terminal, a script, CI): use `upload_media`. If the user says they cannot see a picker, fall back to `upload_media` and do not call this again. IN THE SAME REPLY: say the picker is open (it takes several files in turn), ask what the task still needs (what happens in the clip, or what the file is for), and stop: no polling, no `upload_media` or `confirm_upload`. When the user answers, take the newest url of the right kind from `list_uploads` (none: upload unfinished, say so). ACCEPTED TYPES: `video/mp4` and `video/quicktime` up to 50 MB; `image/png`, `image/jpeg` and `image/webp` up to 20 MB; the picker refuses anything else before a byte moves. WebM, AVIF, HEIC, TIFF and GIF are not accepted: re-encode to MP4 or PNG / JPEG. Costs no tokens (the upload uses the account's rolling 24-hour media allowance). OUTPUT: a short JSON list of accepted types, for the card: do not paste it.
name: upload_media_widget
title: Open a file picker in the conversation
